item.title: The Alejandro Mario Yllanes Paintings Saved From a Dumpster
item.description: Alejandro Mario Yllanes, a self-taught Bolivian painter, made searingly political works championed by Diego Rivera. Their journey to major museums is a 50-year saga full of mysteries.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Burnett
item.media:credit: Nic Antaya for The New York Times
item.media:description: “Lake Titicaca” by Alejandro Mario Yllanes will hang at the Toledo Museum of Art in Ohio. The painting was one of about a dozen found in a dumpster around 1978.

item.title: He Asked ‘Why Such a Nice Girl Would Paint Such Wild Pictures.’ The Rest Is Art History.
item.description: Gallerists have uncovered rare works by Marguerite and William Zorach, shining light on the pioneering collaborators. Their modern art love story bows at the Independent 20th Century fair.
item.dc:creator: Hilarie M. Sheets

item.title: A Collector’s Art, on Loan to the Met, Will Be Owned by Nigeria
item.description: Novel collaborations with countries of origin allow objects in private U.S. collections to be repatriated and head for the Met on loan.
item.dc:creator: Colin Moynihan

item.title: British Museum Bans Photography of Bayeux Tapestry to Keep Lines Moving
item.description: “Our priority is to ensure that all visitors have the best experience possible,” the museum said about the hottest ticket in London.
item.dc:creator: Amelia Nierenberg and Alex Marshall
item.media:description: Visitors at the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition at the British Museum.

item.title: New Bid to Claim Cranach Paintings Held by Norton Simon Museum
item.description: Courts have upheld the museum’s title to the paintings once looted by the Nazis, but a lawsuit seeks to press forward with the claim under a new California law.
item.dc:creator: Nina Siegal

item.title: Two Centuries On, Smithsonian Connects Jefferson’s Hair to Hemings’s Children
item.description: A new book describes how cutting-edge genomics techniques yielded “extraordinary proof” that Thomas Jefferson fathered children with Sally Hemings.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Schuessler
item.category: History by a Hair: Thomas Jefferson, Sally Hemings & Solving a 200-Year-Old Mystery (Book)

item.title: The Midcareer Artist Camille Henrot Is Apparently Tireless
item.description: The French artist makes you feel like a reveler in her epiphanies, from slapstick commedia dell’arte to dog sculptures in Central Park. At midcareer she is apparently tireless.
item.dc:creator: Walker Mimms
item.media:credit: Sam Hellmann for The New York Times

item.title: Weird and Wonderful, the Lucas Museum Lands in L.A.
item.description: A billion-dollar behemoth that looks like a spaceship houses the art collection of the “Star Wars” filmmaker George Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson. It’s an instant landmark.
item.dc:creator: Michael Kimmelman
item.media:credit: Jake Michaels for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, with its viewing port window on the gallery floor, overlooks new parkland.

item.title: Peter Max Franchised the Cosmic ’60s Into Commercial Success, Without the Museum
item.description: For decades, his bold colors and benign peace-and-love message captivated those who saw America shining.
item.dc:creator: Jason Farago

item.title: The Wind of Creation Blows Across the Met’s Facade
item.description: The Beijing-based artist Liu Wei, in his new commission, dreams of what lies behind the museum door — and has a bit of fun with it too.
item.dc:creator: Will Heinrich
item.media:credit: Christopher Gregory-Rivera for The New York Times
item.media:description: Liu Wei, visiting from Beijing, takes a break during the installation of his Met Facade Commission, one of four giant hands holding a tower of abstract forms.

item.title: Gordon Parks as His Subjects Knew Him
item.description: Isabella Rossellini, Lonnie Ali, Anderson Cooper and other relatives of those who figured in the celebrated photographer’s portraiture bolster a new exhibition at the Jack Shainman Gallery.
item.dc:creator: Reggie Ugwu

item.title: Heirs Sue Auschwitz Museum Over Art Their Mother Made Under the Nazis
item.description: Josef Mengele, the “Angel of Death” doctor, ordered Dina Gottliebova Babbitt, an Auschwitz prisoner, to create watercolor paintings. Her daughters want them back.
item.dc:creator: Robin Pogrebin

item.title: Arthur Jafa, Art’s Great Disrupter, Readies a ‘Big Bang’
item.description: “I Am Tony,” the artist’s largest museum survey to date, carries a powerful message about identity “forged in the holds of slave ships.”
item.dc:creator: Holland Cotter and Gioncarlo Valentine
item.media:credit: Gioncarlo Valentine for The New York Times

item.title: Art Gallery Shows to See in September
item.description: This week in Newly Reviewed, Max Lakin covers Sara Anstis’s’s unsettling mystery, Yvonne Jacquette’s aerial views and George Rouy’s sobering turn.
item.dc:creator: Max Lakin, Carolina A. Miranda and Will Heinrich

item.title: Adam Pendleton Is Painting the White Cube Black
item.description: On Oct. 10, the artist’s exhibition, “Some Wild Kind of Language,” opens at the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam. It will upend expectations.
item.dc:creator: Nina Siegal
item.media:credit: Clifford Prince King for The New York Times
item.media:description: Adam Pendleton with his painting “The Door (A Days Painting),” 2026, which will be at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam.

item.title: Swivel Chairs You’ll Want to Give a Whirl
item.description: Unexpected colors and textures put a new spin on rotating seats.

item.title: At the V&A’s Schiaparelli Show, More Than Just Showstopping Gowns
item.description: One of the designer’s earliest patrons was an Australian woman who defied convention to marry into Indian royalty.
item.dc:creator: Divya Venkataraman

item.title: Was Mary Magdalene a Sinner or a Saint? Artists Weigh In
item.description: A new exhibition at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt traces her shifting image over the centuries.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Bahr
item.media:description: “Mary Magdalene: Sin. Pray. Love,” includes over 100 paintings, sculptures and works on paper from around 60 institutions across Europe and North America, including “Penitent Magdalen in Meditation,” by Georges de La Tour (1635-40).

item.title: Florian Krewer, a German-Born New York Painter, Explores the Spaces Between
item.description: Florian Krewer’s arresting images have earned him yet another solo show, this time at the Musée d’Art Moderne de Paris.
item.dc:creator: Ted Loos
item.media:credit: Oliver Farshi for The New York Times
item.media:description: Florian Krewer at his studio in the Bronx, N.Y., in August

item.title: In Brazil, a Museum Renovation Celebrates Overlooked Artists
item.description: The Museum of Modern Art in São Paulo reopens this month with the 39th edition of the Panorama of Brazilian Art, a showcase of the country’s work.
item.dc:creator: Ray Mark Rinaldi
item.category: Museum of Modern Art (Sao Paulo, Brazil)

item.title: In India, Studio Raw Material Create a Highly Modern Home From Ancient Materials
item.description: For a weekend house near Makrana, a pair of designers relied on local marble and traditional masonry.
item.dc:creator: Aatish Nath and Mikael Olsson

item.title: Inside Peter Schlesinger’s Long Island Home
item.description: The 19th-century Long Island home that Peter Schlesinger shared with his late husband, Eric Boman, nearly defies the passage of time.
item.dc:creator: Nick Haramis and Jason Schmidt

item.title: In the Swiss Alps, a Sprawling-but-Cozy Chalet Designed by Billy Cotton
item.description: For his first European project, the American designer Billy Cotton recast a home in Gstaad as a vibrant family retreat.
item.dc:creator: Laura May Todd and Mikael Olsson

item.title: Inside Stine Gam and Enrico Fratesi’s Home on the Italian Coast
item.description: At their 19th-century farmhouse on the Italian coast, the duo behind GamFratesi blend modern Scandinavian simplicity with Mediterranean warmth.
item.dc:creator: Laura May Todd, Henry Bourne and Tom Delavan

item.title: How Hauvette and Madani Brought Easy Charm to a Classic Haussmannian Apartment in Paris
item.description: Samantha Hauvette and Lucas Madani created a home that reflects the city’s history — and their own.
item.dc:creator: Kurt Soller and Thibault Montamat

item.title: Inside Stephen Antonakos’s Neon-Lit SoHo Apartment
item.description: In the 1960s, having discovered a deep affection for the material, the artist Stephen Antonakos transformed his SoHo home into a kaleidoscopic fever dream.

item.title: Inside David Alhadeff and Jason Duzansky’s L.A. Home Filled With Priceless Objects and a Young Child
item.description: When the Tudor Revival became available, a creative couple and their son moved out of their design gallery and embraced a freer, more personal way of living.
item.dc:creator: Alice Newell-Hanson and Ben Lindbloom

item.title: What Does a House Tell Us About Its Occupants?
item.description: Taste and materials can reveal more than we might expect.

item.title: New Home for Aperture Photography Center
item.description: The Upper West Side headquarters features a bookstore and gallery for exhibitions and discussions.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Lubow

item.title: Conjuring a Herd of Buffalo From Steel, Wood and Burlap
item.description: Over the summer, 40 life-size bison puppets were handmade at St. Ann’s Warehouse in Brooklyn. This weekend, they’ll stampede through New York.
item.dc:creator: Laura Collins-Hughes and Paola Chapdelaine
item.category: Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi (Exhibit)
item.media:description: “Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi” is a free public art spectacle that will wind through Lower Manhattan and Downtown Brooklyn this weekend.

item.title: New York Performing Arts Library Gets $60 Million Gift for Preservation
item.description: The anonymous donation, the library’s largest ever, will support digitization of archival items related to theater, dance and music.

item.title: Trump Administration Outlines Plan for Signs Outside Smithsonian Museum
item.description: In a letter, the Interior Department detailed what it hoped to convey on 12 signs to be installed outside the National Museum of American History.
item.dc:creator: Robin Pogrebin
item.media:description: The Trump administration is pushing forward with a plan to install signs outside the National Museum of American History to warn visitors of the content inside.
